new_statements.citation: Maier, Jacqueline G. 1969. Cua phonemes. Mon-Khmer Studies 3: 9-19.
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Opened (page image of MKS 3 p. 14 from; the PDF is image-only, pages 9-19 map to scanned/p-01..p-11). The page header reads "14... MAIER"; below the final-consonant list the headings are "2. The Phonological Word" / "2.1 Word Pattern" (the misreads the section digits as "9."), and the text is exactly: "The word is composed of one non-obligatory presyllable and the obligatory main syllable, which receives the heavier stress." Verbatim match to the reported quote. Context on the same page: "2.1.1 Presyllable: CV is the only pattern, thus becoming C1 V1 of the word"; "2.1.2 Main Syllable: The two established patterns for the simple word are: C2V2±C5 and C3 C4 V2±C5"; "2.2.1 Within…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Cua words are at most sesquisyllabic: an optional CV presyllable (vowel always a neutralized central a) plus an obligatory main syllable (C)CV(C). Stress falls on the main syllable, i.e. the last syllable of the phonological word; the presyllable is unstressed. Typical Mon-Khmer iambic word shape.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not mentioned; the presyllable is implicitly the lighter syllable ('heavier stress' on the main syllable).
new_statements.exceptions: None stated. 43% of collected words have presyllables, some functioning as affixes (§2.3.1); compounds and phrases are not discussed.
new_statements.domain_note: Phonological word as Maier defines it (presyllable + main syllable). Data from the Tra Bong Valley dialect, 1964-66, ~1700-word dictionary; impressionistic, no instrumental data. The language has no tone or vowel register (Smith 1973:114).
new_statements.identity_note: Maier 1969 describes the Tra Bong Valley dialect (Kool Dong, 'Valley Cua'); the High Mountain dialect (Kool Doot / Kool Taal) was inaccessible to her and is not covered. Glottolog cuaa1241 lists no dialect subdivisions; names Cua = Kor = Cor = Kool = Traw = Bong Miew. Smith 1973 and Sidwell 2009 call the group East(ern North) Bahnaric.

sources.quote: The word is composed of one non-obligatory presyllable and the obligatory main syllable, which receives the heavier stress.
sources.note: p. 14 §2.1 Word Pattern: the word = optional presyllable + obligatory main syllable, 'which receives the heavier stress'; presyllable is CV with a neutralized central vowel only. No other stress remarks; no tone/register.
